title: Deep Learning Model for Obtaining Spatially Resolved Pair Distribution Functions from 4DSTEM Data
content: Amorphous materials are critical components of diverse technologies such as batteries, data storage, and photovoltaics [1]. Understanding the structure and ordering of these materials is a necessary step in understanding their fundamental physical properties and developing next generation materials. Electron diffraction data contains short-range ordering information of amorphous samples, and four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) can probe this order with sub-nanometer resolution [2, 3]. The pair distribution function (PDF) can be reconstructed by averaging and fitting the radial component of the diffraction pattern, and this has proven useful for studies ranging from supercooled water to metallic nanoparticles [4, 5]. These methods, however, are very sensitive to multiple scattering, and it is difficult to apply them quantitatively or to thick samples. They additionally require the manual selection of background fitting parameters. These can be difficult to optimize and greatly impact the results both quantitatively and qualitatively. These constraints also impose limitations on the imaging conditions that further reduce the spatial resolution, even before averaging the individual diffraction patterns. To overcome these limitations, we have trained a deep learning model that can extract pair distribution functions directly from individual diffraction patterns. This will enable new studies of spatially varied short-range order.
